key_insight: DoAtlas-2 is a self-evolving biomedical discovery framework that uses population evidence and causal reasoning to generate, test, and refine mechanistic hypotheses.
clinical_relevance: It may help researchers uncover interpretable disease pathways and support more transparent risk prediction, especially for vascular and metabolic conditions.
method: Integrates 771 research resources spanning clinical, imaging, physiological, and molecular data.
Builds an evidence network from about 4.7 million literature-derived records across 93,566 concepts.
Autonomously proposes causal questions, prespecifies study designs, and updates mechanisms using validation results.
evidence_signal: The system was evaluated on 2,031 research questions; in the Human Phenotype Project, 756 of the first 1,079 screened pathway questions were statistically supported.
watch_item: Because the framework depends on literature-derived evidence and population data, results may reflect underlying data quality, coverage gaps, and residual confounding.
paper_title: DoAtlas-2: A Foundation for Self-Evolving Causal Biomedical Discovery
